packageRules.description: Only runtime/peer bumps of published packages are user-facing: 'fix' makes dependency-changesets-action add a patch changeset; everything else stays 'chore' and gets none.
Published packages bring their map library with them, so consumers only see these bumps through xtramaps releases. 'bump' moves the range floor so every update is a real change for consumers.
A major bump of a framework mirrored as peer + devDependency widens the peer range, but Renovate takes the commit type from the devDependency upgrade.

rlayers pins its ol peer exactly, and Renovate doesn't read peer dependencies. Updating both together means the PR stays red (npm refuses the install) while ol is ahead of rlayers, and turns green once an rlayers release catches up.
@cesium/widgets depends on @cesium/engine; if the two drift apart, npm installs a second engine and the widgets run against a different Cesium instance than the viewer.
Patch bumps are low-risk and covered by CI (lint/build/typecheck/test) - merge automatically once checks pass. Requires 'build' to be a required status check in this repo's branch protection.

Minor/major bumps (incl. maplibre-gl, @maplibre/*, @vis.gl/react-maplibre) need a manual browser check before merging - CI alone doesn't yet cover enough of the map-rendering surface to trust these unattended. Revisit once test coverage for web-map-maplibre(-react) is broader.
